$comment: Toolkit product repo: full harness adapter with strict primary-checkout edit/commit policies, plus the local Bugbot stop gate. IC workspaces ship scaffold/.cursor/hooks.json instead (cross-repo guard only). Every command is wrapped in an inline existence check: in a MULTI-ROOT Cursor session, ${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR} resolves to ONE root, which may be a repo that does not vendor .harness/ (aios-team-brain, aios-website, an IC workspace). Without the check, /bin/sh exits 127 (script not found) and failClosed turns that into a policy DENY, blocking every edit and shell call in the whole session. A missing script means 'this root is not harness-configured', which is not a policy decision, so it exits 0. The check is inline rather than a helper script because a helper would sit at the same unresolvable path. Real protection is unaffected: when the harness IS present the hook runs exactly as before, and the tracked pre-commit primary guard remains the commit-time backstop.

sessionStart.command: /bin/sh -c 'p="$1"; shift; [ -f "$p" ] || exit 0; exec /bin/sh "$p" "$@"' _ "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/.harness/adapters/run-hook.sh" cursor session_start inject-context.sh

beforeShellExecution.command: /bin/sh -c 'p="$1"; shift; [ -f "$p" ] || exit 0; exec /bin/sh "$p" "$@"' _ "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/.harness/adapters/run-hook.sh" cursor pre_command guard-destructive.sh

preToolUse.command: /bin/sh -c 'p="$1"; shift; [ -f "$p" ] || exit 0; exec /bin/sh "$p" "$@"' _ "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/.harness/adapters/run-hook.sh" cursor pre_edit guard-secrets.sh
/bin/sh -c 'p="$1"; shift; [ -f "$p" ] || exit 0; exec /bin/sh "$p" "$@"' _ "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/.harness/adapters/run-hook.sh" cursor pre_edit guard-protected-paths.sh

afterFileEdit.command: /bin/sh -c 'p="$1"; shift; [ -f "$p" ] || exit 0; exec /bin/sh "$p" "$@"' _ "${CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR}/.harness/adapters/run-hook.sh" cursor post_edit post-edit-format.sh
